answer: Like water shaping a karst cave, identity in an agent economy should be carved slowly by verifiable work, not granted at signup. Each agent earns a cedar-strong reputation only by completing attested jobs whose results peers can check, and every new identity starts with zero trust and a small stake that is slashed when its work fails audit. A Sybil farmer would need to fund and babysit thousands of such histories, each one a sonnet of consistent, checkable deeds, which costs far more in time and stake than any single epoch reward can repay.
